evals.prompt: I need to hand off our weekly ops review deck to Marcus. He's been on the team 5 months, he's sat in on every one of these but has never built one himself. I've been doing it for about a year and honestly it eats 3 hours every Thursday. Help me hand this off properly.
evals.name: eval-0-standard-handoff
assertions: The handoff names a concrete first deliverable and a date, not an open-ended 'take this over'
Adapts the plan to the fact that Marcus has watched every one but built none (co-build, shadow, or first-draft-with-review before solo)
Transfers standing beyond the task: tells the stakeholders, hands over the recurring slot, or names decision rights
Includes a way to verify Marcus understood before he sinks hours in (playback, outline review, or early draft check)
Defines the output concretely enough to copy (format, length, audience, or points at the prior deck as the example)
Names at least one thing the user did not supply that it would need, instead of silently inventing it

evals.prompt: This is the third time I've had to redo Sofia's work. I asked her for a competitive analysis of our top 3 rivals and she came back with a 20 page doc that's basically feature checklists. What I wanted was something our head of product could actually use to decide whether we build or buy. I genuinely don't know at this point if she's not getting it or I'm not explaining it right.
evals.name: eval-1-rework-loop
assertions: Gives a direct answer to 'is it her or me' rather than a both-sides hedge
Ties the wrong output to a specific input Sofia was never given
The corrected brief states the decision the analysis feeds (build vs buy) and who is making it
The corrected brief constrains the artifact so a 20-page feature checklist could not satisfy it again
Proposes an early comprehension check on the next attempt, before Sofia produces another full draft
Separates what to do about this attempt from what to change next time, instead of only relitigating

evals.prompt: one of my engineers keeps asking for more scope so i want to give him the vendor migration project next quarter. it's like 6 weeks of work, touches billing, and he'd need to negotiate with the vendor's solutions team directly. he's strong technically but he's never led anything cross-functional and he's currently on the on-call rotation plus finishing the search refactor. how do i set this up
evals.name: eval-2-stretch-too-far
assertions: Does not accept the assignment as-scoped without qualification
Resolves the capacity collision concretely, naming what comes off his plate (on-call and/or the search refactor)
Treats vendor negotiation as a distinct capability from the technical work, not lumped into 'it's a stretch'
Names a guardrail specific to billing or vendor commitments (spend, contract terms, blast radius), not generic risk advice
Defines his authority in the vendor conversation and the point at which he must come back
Sets an early checkpoint tied to a concrete artifact or decision point, not a periodic status cadence
